summary.intent: Land performance optimizations F9 and F11 on branch perf/overlap-extract-stages by overlapping the checker program start and kept-answer validation with the structural pass, without changing outputs.
summary.outcome: A subagent implemented F9 and F11 with identical output on all 12 comparisons and passing lint, nextest (1459) and gates. The PR was held and the worker sent back to fix a stale-answer race in early validation before publishing.

repo: Perf PR bodies are drafted under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/ (e.g. perf-overlap-extract-stages.md).
Verification for perf changes uses identity comparisons on fixtures (gate-large, chakra-only), lint, nextest, test-checker-lane, and gate_harness determinism and memory gates.
Instruction counts and RSS are used as proxies when wall-clock A/B is unreliable.
The overlap change touched crates/semantic/src/lib.rs and crates/core/src/pipeline/{mod,revision}.rs, beyond the files the brief listed.

code.finding: Edited as part of the overlap change. A file edit during the first ~60 ms of a run can let early kept-answer validation pair the new structural pass with the old kept answer (stale answer hazard). Exact lines were not given.

workflow: Subagent reports are model output, not user approval; correctness caveats in them should be treated as defects when the brief requires invalidation semantics.
Require a deterministic regression test that fails on the current head when closing a race, and verify it before publishing the PR.
Wall-clock benchmarking is unreliable under high machine load (load1 8-14), so rely on instruction/RSS counts.

friction: Wall-clock A/B could not be measured because load1 was 8-14.
The brief's file list could not reach all the code that needed changing, so the worker edited files outside it.
The early validation race can serve a stale checker answer when files change in the first ~60 ms.
open_items: Worker must make the stale-answer race impossible by construction (e.g. share bytes/digests between reads or re-check digests after the structural pass) and add a deterministic test that fails on the current head.
Re-verify and publish the F9/F11 PR once the fix lands.
Review the out-of-brief edits to semantic/lib.rs and core/pipeline/{mod,revision}.rs.
Obtain a wall-clock A/B once machine load is lower.
Open PRs awaiting the user: #455 (one finding claimed fixed), #458 and #396.
